title: Do Phones Hurt Test Scores?
intro: A school newspaper published this report last week.
body: Students at Lincoln Middle School who spend more time on their phones get lower test scores. Our survey of 200 students found that students with more than 4 hours of daily screen time averaged 71% on their math final, while students with less than 1 hour averaged 88%. The evidence is clear: phones are damaging student learning. The school should ban phones during school hours to raise test scores.

chart.alt: Scatter chart showing daily screen time in hours against math final score, with a downward trend.

regions.caption: The downward trend line running across the plotted student data points.
The vertical axis showing math final score, which starts at 60 rather than 0.
A cluster of students with high screen time who still scored above 85.
The footnote reading 'Self-reported screen time, 200 students, single class period'.

transcript.text: Reporter: We asked students how long they spend on their phones each day.
Student: I guess maybe two hours? I never really counted.
Reporter: The survey was handed out during a single third period class.
Principal: These numbers make the case for a phone ban on their own.

opening_prompt: Read the report and look at the chart. What is one question you would ask before believing this conclusion? You can highlight text or click part of the chart to point at what you mean.
